stages.journal: Never-Sold, who keeps the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, told me of Ussa-Rekh, who bought out Owings for thirty years and now hires out the crews he freed on the docks at Soulrest. Heavy-Rope, the boss of one of those crews, sent word to the Chainbreakers about him. I'm to find Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock at Soulrest, a short way east of Lilmoth along the coast.

Heavy-Rope, the boss of a dock crew at Soulrest, told me his crew asked Ussa-Rekh to let them end their last season of hire early, and Ussa-Rekh refused. I'm to hear Ussa-Rekh's side; he stands just along the dock from Heavy-Rope.

Ussa-Rekh told me on the Soulrest docks that he freed these crews and that they work the season as agreed. He says the crews' hire stopped paying for further buy-outs the year the berths he bought for them began to cost more than that hire. I'm to tell Heavy-Rope whether I stand with his crew, who want out of the last season, or with Ussa-Rekh, who holds them to it.

I told Heavy-Rope on the Soulrest docks that I stand with his crew. Ussa-Rekh keeps their carved tokens until the last season is worked, and a crew holding its own tokens owes him nothing more. Heavy-Rope gave me the crew's coin for that season, 50 gold, mine to keep if words get the tokens. I'm to get the tokens from Ussa-Rekh, just along the dock: talk him round, or pay him.
I talked Ussa-Rekh round on the Soulrest docks, and he gave me the crew's carved tokens without the crew's coin. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.

I paid Ussa-Rekh on the Soulrest docks the crew's own coin for their last season, 50 gold, as if they had worked it, and he gave me their carved tokens. I'm to give the tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock.

I told Heavy-Rope at the head of the Soulrest dock that I stand with Ussa-Rekh and that his crew should take the refusal and work the season out. Heavy-Rope will not take it from a stranger without a reason worth hearing. I'm to talk him round, or pay 50 gold for his crew's lost days.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Heavy-Rope's crew against Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed them and hires them still. I got their carved tokens from Ussa-Rekh and gave them to Heavy-Rope. A crew holding its own tokens owes Ussa-Rekh nothing more, and Heavy-Rope's crew will not work for him again.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and talked Heavy-Rope into taking his refusal. The crew will work their last season under Ussa-Rekh.

On the Soulrest docks I stood with Ussa-Rekh, the broker who freed Heavy-Rope's crew and hires them still, and paid Heavy-Rope 50 gold for his crew's lost days to take the refusal. The crew will work their last season under Ussa-Rekh.
Heavy-Rope or Ussa-Rekh is dead. The matter of the Soulrest crew's last season will never be settled now. I have no more to do in it.

Hear Ussa-Rekh on the dock at Soulrest, just along from Heavy-Rope.
Tell Heavy-Rope which side to stand with, his crew's or Ussa-Rekh's.
Get the crew's carved tokens from Ussa-Rekh: persuade him (Speechcraft 30), or pay him the crew's 50 gold.
Give the carved tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock at Soulrest.
Give the carved tokens to Heavy-Rope at the head of the dock at Soulrest.
Persuade Heavy-Rope to take Ussa-Rekh's refusal (Speechcraft 30), or pay him 50 gold for his crew's lost days.

lines.speaker: npc.mercantile-coast.soulrest.crew-boss
lines.prompt: What is wrong with your crew?
lines.text: Never-Sold has told you what we asked of Ussa-Rekh and what he answered. I will tell you why we asked. A master in Lilmoth, a short way west along the coast, offers my crew berths of our own from the new season, if we come free of Ussa-Rekh first. The master will not hold them for us through another season. I owe Ussa-Rekh my freedom. He bought me out of my Owing, and I say so to anyone who asks. That is why this galls me. A man who has seen what a debt does should not hold us to a season we do not want. He stands a few steps along the dock. Hear him as well as me.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose-prison.chainbreaker-envoy-camped-causeway
lines.prompt: Tell me about the dock crews.
lines.text: An Owing is a debt that a person works off in labour. I buy out the people held, one at a time. I pay for the next one with the crews' hire. I will tell you plainly when that stopped working. It stopped the year the berths that I bought for the crews began to cost me more than their hire. A crew that goes early leaves me the berth's price to carry. With that price unpaid I can buy out no more Owings. The person held on an estate stays held. I hold that a season agreed is a season worked. So do the estates. Heavy-Rope, just along the dock, can tell you what his crew asked of me. I refused it for the reason I have given.

If coin is what moves him, pay him with it. If your words get the tokens from him, keep the gold.

lines.text: The crew works the season for Ussa-Rekh, as you wished. We will do the work. Do not ask me to thank you for it.

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose-prison.chainbreaker-envoy-camped-causeway

lines.speaker: npc.imperial-penal-south.blackrose-prison.chainbreaker-envoy-camped-causeway
lines.text: You kept the season. I do not forget who made that so. It was not kind to Heavy-Rope. I know it.

lines: Easy water, traveller, but keep your eyes open to the south-south-east. A bear and her cubs roam a short way off that way, and a Tree Mother lives in the woods there too. Stay clear of both.
The Dwemer Ruin, traveller? Easy enough. Walk south-east from here a short way and you are standing in it.

Alten Merihall, traveller? Walk south-east a short way, until the Dwemer Ruin is on your left, and then keep south-east a fair way. Alten Merihall is there, and the money with it. There is a water route too, for those who prefer boats.
Lilmoth Dock, traveller? Walk west a short way, until the big ship is on your left, and then climb west a fair way. The dock is there.
Easy water, my friend! Sit by me a while. There is room on the landing. I chose Soulrest over Lilmoth Dock because there is no licence to be shown here. Now I have good company besides.
Easy water, traveller. This is Soulrest, and I run a boat from the landing here. Where are you going, and do you need a boat to get there?
Soulrest is where the boats tie up, traveller. Mine is one of them. A large ship lies west of here, a short way to the west-south-west, with a door aboard if you want to look inside.

Lilmoth fell, traveller. The outside traders went elsewhere after that. Alten Merihall's merchants have taken much of the bay's trade since then. That is where the money is now. I would carry you there gladly.

Heavy-Rope leads a crew on Soulrest's dock. The crew want their season ended early, traveller. The broker who hires them out will not hear of it. I only watch from the landing, so go and ask Heavy-Rope yourself.
I am Seeks-The-Channel, and I run a boat out of Soulrest, east of Lilmoth Dock. I wait here at the head of the landing between fares. I chose this place because no licence is asked for here.
You are back, my friend. Come to the stall. I will sell you what I have at last season's price, and not a coin more.
Outsider. Buy something or move along. Do not touch the goods.
Gourds grow just north-north-west of this stall. Pick your own. Mine are for sale.
This is Soulrest. Houses open onto it, one just south of me and another just south-east. Keep your hands off the doors, outsider.
I am Ushaa-Mei. I sell food here on the south-west side, between the houses. I remember what everything cost last season, so do not try to argue.
Food and small goods. I sell them at last season's price. I weigh it fair and I expect the coin to be good.
Plaits-The-Reed sits just west of me. I like her. Ask her yourself.
Hello again! Sit by the fire with me, and I will tell you what the grown-ups said today.
Hello, sir. Or miss. Please, do you smile?
Deathbell, nightshade, jazbay and other flowers grow together, miss. They are just south-east of here.
This is Soulrest, sir. Two cows graze just east-north-east of here, and Cow-Chaser scares them on purpose. Then he says it was me.
I am Little-Gecko. I sit in the middle, sir, where the grown-ups talk, so I hear everything. One day I will be a boat captain.
Seeks-The-Channel, the boat captain, stands just east of here. She is the best captain there is. Feldril Nethri, the Dunmer, works just north-east. He is kind to me, miss.
A Vale Deer lies dead just south-east of here, child. Something killed it. I would not go looking for the cause.
Child, you came back. Sit by me, out of the wind, and let me look at your hands. Tell me how you are.
Mind the reeds, child. I have not finished with them yet.
Glowing mushrooms and creep cluster grow under the trees, a short way south of here, child. I do not go that far now.
An Argonian kept long from the Hist grows pale, child. The colour thins and the markings go soft. When they go home, it all comes back.
Careful hands are sometimes of use to Tilts-The-Jug, child. Inside the house on Soulrest's dock, I am told. I always look at a stranger's hands first. Let me see yours.
I am Plaits-The-Reed. I weave mats and baskets for the families here, and for the boats. My husband is out fishing, child. He will be back soon.
Xeeh-Nah works just east-south-east of here. Xeeh-Nah should marry, I always say. Go and see, child.
Warrior! You are here! Did you bring the sword? Show me, show me, I will not touch it.
Hey, warrior! Have you got a sword? Do you have any scars? Show me one!
Gourds? They grow just north-west of here, warrior. I could carry them all myself, but I am busy with the cows.
This is Soulrest, and I am the best fighter in it! Ask the cows. A boar roots a short way north-east of here, and I am going to fight it one day.
I am Cow-Chaser, a hatchling of Soulrest, and I am going to be a warrior! I practise on the cows, because they run and that makes them hard to hit. Do you have a real sword?
Little-Gecko sits just west-south-west of here. Little-Gecko is a baby. Xeeh-Nah works just south of here. Xeeh-Nah is the strongest person alive! Go and see for yourself, warrior.

Go north-west a fair way, until Lilmoth Dock is on your left. Climb west a short way to the big ship on your left. Then west again, a short way, to the dead tree on your left. From there, ask again, ojel. The plantation lies further west.
Kin. Good. Sit by the benches a while. I will move the loads later.
Mm. What do you want, ojel? I have loads to move.
There is a chest by the big ship. It is a short way west-south-west of here. I do not know more than that.
On the big docks they hire a ship's crew with another man's months of owing. The harbourmaster calls it hiring. Free hands lose their paid work to it.
Tilts-The-Jug sometimes wants careful hands, ojel. Mine are for hauling. Try the house on the dock.
I am Xeeh-Nah. I haul cargo and tie up the boats here at Soulrest, on the south-east side. Half the people of Soulrest owe me money.
I carry loads and tie the boats up. The big ship lies a short way west of here. Its door leads aboard.
Ah, it is you. Few people trouble to cross to this end of the room. I do not forget the ones who do. Stay a while, friend.
Well, outlander. You have found the corner of Soulrest where visitors do not come by choice. State your business and I shall tell you whether I can oblige.

This is Soulrest, outlander. I am not permitted by the fire with the families, so I am put at this end. The north door is just west of me and another just east-south-east. The cooking pot stands just south-east, though I would not say I am welcome to it.

Here a debt is paid in work, outlander. An arbitrator turns the loss into months of labour that are counted in nushmeekos. When the months are worked the matter is over, so they say. Once, foreigners without a licence were kept to the docks at Lilmoth and barred from the city.

The crew that Heavy-Rope leads works Soulrest's dock, outlander. They want their season ended early. The broker who hires out their labour refuses. I was a trader once, and I know a broker's terms win over a man's wishes. Ask for Heavy-Rope there.

I am Feldril Nethri, a Dunmer. For now I am a guest of this marsh, though the hospitality has terms. I came to trade. I lost a cargo and was assessed months of labour. I cannot see when they will end, outlander.
There is a child called Little-Gecko, sitting just south-west of here. She is kind to me, which is more than I can say for most under this roof. I would thank you not to trouble her.
The market's cooking fire? It is north-east of here, a short way. Go on, I have boats to watch.
You are back, my friend. The water is quiet, so stay a while and talk.
Speak. I have boats to watch.
This is Black Rose. The south landing's dock is just south of here. A boat lies just south-south-east. I know her hull.
In the Second Era, word went round the coast that Black Rose had fallen and was gone. It was not. It is still here. I watch its landing.
I am Sakeeth. I watch the south landing for boats that do not pay. I grew up hauling nets on these docks. I joined the guard to be issued boots.
Holds-Fast is the guard on the path above the south docks. He is usually just east-north-east of here. I would trust him in a real fight.
The jail. Walk north-east a short way. It is there.
Haven. Walk south-east a short way, round the cliffs, to the boat on its rack. Then walk south-west a short way, past the stone tower. Haven is there.
It is you. Stand by the post a while, my friend. The road is quiet and I am glad of the company.
Stop there. State your business. Let me see what you carry.
The tower is a short way north-north-west of here. Ahkeeh smokes fish in this town. It is the best thing in Black Rose. I stand at the west gate and count what comes through it.
People say many go into Black Rose and few ever leave. Old prison staff, freed prisoners, deserters and runaways all came here and stayed. I have counted a good many of them through this gate.
The dead lie on the road toward Haven. They are Imperials, with an elf among them. The people of Black Rose have not gone to bury them.
I am Tzeel-Vaa, guard at the west gate. I have stood here longer than the two beside me have been alive. My father guarded this same road for the same pay.
Quintel is the other guard at this gate, grandson of an Imperial jailer. He is usually just north-north-east of here. He is too soft for the work.
The cooking fire by the docks? Walk east a short way, and the fire is there. I charge no toll for directions.
You again. Come, stand a while, my friend. For you there is no fee at this gate. I have said that to very few.
The crossing costs coin. I will name the sum once I have seen your pack.
This is the west gate of Black Rose. I keep the toll here. The marker post is just south-south-west of where you stand. Pass it only once the fee is settled.

Around Black Rose, an owing is taken at a crossing for damage to the way. The debtor works it off on the water. I did that myself once, so I know the sum of it better than most. Now I am the one who takes the toll. I will not apologise for the post.

I am Counts-The-Tolls, guard at this gate. I was a debtor once, working off an owing on the water. I took this post as the way out. I know how that sounds, but the post is paid work and the water was not.
Tzeel-Vaa is the oldest of the three guards at this gate. He is usually just south-south-east of here. He watches my hands at every cart. He should have retired years ago. Speak to him if you must.
Black Rose Jail, traveller? It lies north-east of here, a short walk. Go that way and you will come to it.
Ah, it is you. Forgive me if I stand stiffly. It is how I was taught. I am glad to see you at the gate again.
Pardon me, traveller. This is the west gate of Black Rose. State your business. I will help if I am able.
This is Black Rose, traveller. The tower stands a short way north-north-west of here.
The people of Black Rose once sent an envoy to the Imperial court. Emperor Pelagius answered him in grunts and squeaks. I do not enjoy telling it, traveller.
I am Quintel, a guard at the west gate. I carry the name of the Imperial jailer who raised my grandmother. I answer to no other. My family has worn a uniform in Black Rose for three generations.
Ahkeeh, the fish smoker, works at the fire west of the gate. You will usually find Ahkeeh just north-west of here.
Black Rose Jail. Go north-east a short way, until the statue with the sword is on your left. Then north, just a little further. The jail stands there.
I know your step now. Stand with me a while, if you wish.
Speak quietly here. This is a shrine. I do not know you yet.
The standing stone is just south-south-west of here. Go to it slowly. Do not climb on it.
The first city here belonged to the Lilmothiit, the fox-folk. Every one of them died of a fever, long before Argonians claimed this place.
I guard the standing stone. The other guards did not want the post, so I asked for it. The stone is older than this town. I keep it as a shrine.
Mireel is a guard on the path above the south docks. You will usually find Mireel a short way south-east of here. Do not expect much from the guards at the docks.
The longboat? Go along the boards east a short way. The longboat is there.
Sunned and warm? I am glad it is you. I have nothing to report today. Ask me what you like.
Halt. State your business on the boards. I was told to ask every stranger, so I am asking you.
This is the dock walk below the market. I guard it. There is a cooking fire just south-east of here, and the dock is just south.
When the fever came to Murkmire, the last of the Lilmothiit fled inland toward Black Rose. What became of them is not known. Have you seen any of them on the road?

I am Okaw-Sei, guard of the dock walk. I walk the boards between the dock and the market all day. I was told to watch for anything unusual. I am newly hatched to the guard, but I mean to serve it well.
Teeda-Wan, the guard at the market, is the best fighter on the docks. You will usually find Teeda-Wan just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire? Walk south a short way, and you will find it.
Ah, it is you. I am glad of it. Stand by me a while, the road is quiet.
You again. Good. Stay here with me and ask what you like.
Hm. What do you want? Be quick about it.
Keep to the road, stranger. I am watching it.
This is the road below the jail. You will find a house just to the south-east.
There is a house just south-east of us. I keep watch near it.
Hm. I know little of Black Marsh, but I know the Rose. Its families are three generations deep. A newcomer owes the prison-born for shelter. The ledger is kept by people who were born owing.
The Rose has families three generations deep. If you are new there, you owe the prison-born for your shelter. The ledger is kept by those who were born owing.
Xuth-Ma. I guard the road that runs up to the jail. Most days I talk to Dredges-The-Silt, who stops by the house here.
I am a guard on this road. I do not like the jail. I will not say why.
Dredges-The-Silt keeps the town's channels clear. I know no better company. You will usually find the dredger just north-west of here.
You want Dredges-The-Silt, the dredger who clears the town's channels. Look just north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Go south a short way. You cannot miss it.
Still watching that jail, as you see. It is good to talk to someone I trust. I am still waiting for the day it is emptied.
What do you want? I am watching the road below the jail. Keep your hands where I can see them.
The house is just south-west of here. Go and look at it yourself.
The families who hold the Rose say it is their home, not a prison. They take it badly when outsiders call it one. I call it a jail. I do not care who hears me.
I am Wazei. I guard this road. My captain has put me where he can see me, because I have been warned twice for wanting a fight with the keepers up there.
Ruh-Jaal is the guard nearest the jail. You will usually find him just west-north-west of here. Do not expect much of him. He is a coward.
Walk just south until you reach the boat on its rack. Then just south-west, and the cooking fire is there. Keep your voice low about who asked.
Come closer, my friend. Keep your voice down. I hear more on this dock than any other guard. For you I will share it.
Keep your voice low. I do not know your face. I like to know every face on this dock.
You are new here. Who have you been speaking to since you arrived?
Quietly now, though everyone knows it. The dock is just south-south-west of here. A boat lies the same way, just as near.
Quietly now. Ask Quintel about the Imperial court. That is his tale, but I would like to know who else asks him for it.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about the Haven road. I hear everything said on this dock, not what is said elsewhere. I would like to know what he says.
I am Tuh-Weem. I guard this dock. Everything said on it reaches my ears. I am rarely wrong about what I hear.
Mends-The-Hulls mends boats at the north-east dock. She is usually just north-east of here. I think she is courting someone. Ask her yourself.
The longboat? Walk south-east a short way and you will reach it. Mind your boots on the silt.
The water is low this season, so I have time to talk. Stand by me if you like.
Mind where you put your boots. The silt is soft here.
There is a house just south-east of here. That is all I would point out.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about crossings and the owing set there. He has forgotten where he came from, so ask him plainly. I have worked mine off in the silt for nine seasons.
I am Dredges-The-Silt. I clear the channels around Black Rose so the boats can pass. It is owing work. It has taken me nine seasons so far.
Xuth-Ma is the guard on the road to the jail. You will usually find him just south-east of here. He is a good man. He is the one who listens to me in the evenings.
The cooking fire? Go south, a short way. The fire is there.
Keep your voice low, and stand by me a while. I will not mind the company.
Move along, if you please. I am on watch.
The standing stone is just north-west of here. The jail is there too, just beside it. I would not look at it for long.
Ask Wazei about what the families call the Rose. I would rather not say it myself. He is a danger to us all, so keep your voice low when you ask.
I am a guard. I stand nearest the jail and keep my post. That is all there is to say.
Pays-In-Reeds is a reed-weaver. She is kind. You will usually find her just north-north-west of here, working off her owing in mats. Ask her, not me.
Black Rose Jail? You can see it from here. It is just south-west. Do not wander off the way.
The north district is quiet today. I am glad of it. Stay as long as you like.
Keep to the road and keep your voice down. The families here are asleep or at their work.
This is the north district, where the families live. I know every child in it by name. The house is just north-north-west of here.
Ask Sakeeth about the Second Era tale that this town was gone. I guard the north district and leave tales to others.
I am Shaleem. I guard the north district, so mind how you behave in it.
Talks-To-Water is a boat captain in the north district. You will usually find her just east-south-east of here. She should take more care with her boat.
The cooking fire? Everyone knows that. Walk south a short way past the house and you will be standing at it. I could find it with my eyes shut.
I have been watching the water for boats all day! Do you want to hear what I have noticed?
You are new here, are you not? I notice everyone new. Where did you come from? Did you come by boat?
This is the north district. I know all of it. The house is just east-north-east of here. Nobody knows this place better than me.
I am Zeeki. I am the cleverest child in the north district. Ask anyone. One day I will captain a boat of my own.
Talks-To-Water, the boat captain? That is the best captain there is. You will usually find the captain just west-south-west of here. One day I will have a place on that boat.
The cooking fire? A sweet first. Go south-east a short way. You will see the fire.
Did you bring a sweet? I have heard things at the jail, and I will tell you them.
Who are you? Stay where I can see you. Have you got a sweet?
The standing stone is just south of here. The tower is just north-north-west. I like sweets better than talking.
I am Skink. I play by the standing stone, where the other children do not come. I have no family. I hear things at the jail. I tell them for a sweet.
Pays-In-Reeds is nice. She weaves reeds into mats to work off what she owes. She is usually just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire by the docks? Listen, water, a stranger wants to walk. Go just south-east until you reach the house. Then go south a short way, and the cooking fire is there.
I told the water you would return. Come, sit by it and tell me what you have seen.
You have the look of someone who does not know the water. What do you want?
Quiet, little ripples, we have a guest. The house is just south-south-east of here. I keep my boat at the north landing.
Long ago the bandit king Red Bramman ruled this country. He raided Topal Bay from here. The First Empire hunted him for years.

Hush, water. You ask for news, stranger. In the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district, Never-Sold has saved coin to buy a woman free of her Owing at the estate north of Blackrose. Never-Sold is asking for a hand with it.
I am Talks-To-Water. I captain a boat out of the north landing. Yes, I talk to the water. My crew is used to it.
Zeeki, the child of the north district, is usually just east-north-east of here. That one should be a sailor. I have said so.
The cooking fire? Go just south, until the longboat is on your left. Then along the boards, just west. The fire is there.
If you have a boat that leaks, bring it to me and I will patch it today.
You are welcome here. Mind the boards, they are wet. What needs mending?
What do you want? I have hulls to patch.
Speak quickly. I am in the middle of a hull.
My house is just north-east of here. The dock is just east-north-east, where the small boats tie up.
Just north-east is my house. Just east-north-east is the dock. I patch the boats there.
If you want something to do, Never-Sold needs a hand. The money is ready to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. Ask at the Chainbreakers' house in the north district.
I am Mends-The-Hulls. I patch the small boats at the north-east dock, cheap and fast. My mother taught me the trade. She learned it working off an owing.
I mend hulls. Pitch-Pot says my work is careless, but Pitch-Pot is slow and expensive. My patches hold.
Tuh-Weem is the guard at the north-east boat dock. He is usually just south-west of here. He should mind his own dock.
You want Tuh-Weem, the guard at the north-east boat dock. As a rule he is just south-west of here. Go and ask him.
Black Rose Jail is a short way to the north-west of here. Eat before you go.
There you are, my friend. Sit down and eat. You look thin to me. The pot is hot.
If you want food, say so. If you do not, I have a pot to watch.
This is Black Rose. My cooking fire is just north-west of here, and the dock is just north-north-east. You have not eaten today, I think.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about who goes into Black Rose and who stays. I came on a prison barge as its cook, and I never got back on it. Have you eaten?
I am Weeska. I cook at the fire and feed the dock hands. Sit, or move along.
Lux Ha mends nets at the market dock, usually just south-south-west of here. Lux Ha works too hard. I doubt that one has eaten.
The longboat? Just east of here, in plain sight. You cannot miss it.
Look at what the boats brought in today. If you have something to sell, I will give you a fair price.
Stranger. Buying or selling? I deal in both.
You want something. Say what it is, or show me what you carry.
The market is where the trade is. The cooking fire is just west-north-west of my stall, and the dock is just north-north-east.
I am Nuxi-Ra. I sell odds and ends here, whatever the boats bring in. I buy from every crew and I do not ask where a thing came from.
Nuxi-Ra. I trade here at the market.
I buy and I sell. My stall is at the market, by the cooking fire. My stock is whatever the boats bring in. Show me what you have and I will name a price.
Rows-Against-It captains a boat from the market dock, and is usually just south-south-west of here. Of all the captains, that is the one who pays on time.
Follow the boards north-east a short way, and you will find the longboat.
Calm water today, and a fare I know. My boat is yours if you need her.
You want a crossing, say where. If not, I have rope to mend.
My boat is just south of here. The dock is just south-east, so mind your feet on the boards.
Ask Okaw-Sei about the last of the Lilmothiit. I carry fares, not old stories. If you want a crossing, say where.
I am Rows-Against-It. I run this boat from the market dock to wherever a fare will go. I paid off my owing on the water and kept the boat. No crossing-keeper gives me orders now.
Weeska cooks at the market fire. She is usually just north-east of here.
The jail. North, a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. Stand by the fire and watch the market with me.
Show me your hands. Then say what you want.
Yes. What do you want?
This is the market. The cooking fire is just south of here. So is the dock. Keep the peace and you will have no trouble from me.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the families of the Rose. He talks of it. I do not.
Teeda-Wan. I keep the peace at this market. That is all.
Lux Ha works the nets on the market dock. Usually just east-south-east of here. Lux Ha should be paid more.
The longboat. Yes. Walk south-east a short way, until you reach the house on your left. Then walk south a short way more. The longboat is there.
Hm. Stand with me a while. I am in no hurry. I am glad it is you.
You wish to speak with me? Then speak. I am Iron-Jaw. I guard the north district.
Hm. There is the house, just there, just north-north-west of where we stand.
Hm. Ask Quintel about Emperor Pelagius. I would like to read his tale in a book one day.
I am Iron-Jaw. A cudgel struck my face in my first year. The name stayed with me. I have stood in the north district ever since. I can read well.
Shaleem is the person you want. Shaleem is a guard in the north district. He is the best guard in the town. You will usually find Shaleem just south-south-east of here.
The cooking fire? South, a fair way past Black Rose. It is there.
Come and stand with me by the boats a while. I could use the company.
I do not know you. Why are you at the landing?
You are a stranger here. Keep clear of the boats.
A boat lies just north-north-west of here. A rowing boat lies just north.
Black Rose and Lilmoth have been rivals for as long as anyone has kept count. I am a guard, not a teller of old tales.
I am Raxa-Tum. I guard the north landing, where the fishing boats tie up. I was a fisher myself once.
Okeemu is the best fisher in town. You will usually find Okeemu just south-west of here, at the north landing.
The jail. Walk south-west a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
You have come up the road again, my friend. I keep the road, as ever. Speak if you wish.
State your business on the north road.
Halt. Say what you want. I am on watch.
This is the north road into Black Rose. The northern marker post is just south of here. A boat lies just east-south-east.
I keep watch here, above the northern marker post. The post is just south. There is a boat just east-south-east of where we stand.

In Empress Morihatha's day the people of Black Rose raised an army against the Empire. Her battlemage Welloc broke it with a spell, not with soldiers. In the town, nobody has trusted a battlemage since.
I am Watches-The-Road. I guard the north road into town. I report every lapse I see. That includes the lapses of other guards.
I am a guard. I watch the north road and I report what I find.
Raxa-Tum, the guard at the north landing, is usually just north-north-west of here. He fishes on duty. He should be dismissed.
The cooking fire? Walk south a fair way, past the house. You will find it there.
The water is good today. Sit by me a while.
I am fishing, so please speak softly.
This is the north landing of Black Rose. My boat is just north-north-east of here.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the Lilmothiit. I know the water and the fish. That is enough for me.
I am Okeemu. I fish from the north landing with my family. My boat is the oldest at the landing.
Heshra, the fishwife at the north landing, is usually just west of here.

Walk south-east just until you reach Black Rose on your left. Then walk south a short way until you reach the statue on your left. Walk south-east just until you reach the house on your left, then south a short way more. The longboat is there.
For you I will not haggle. Come closer and look at the catch.
What do you want? If you are buying, say what you want and what you will pay.
This is the north landing, where I gut and sell the catch. The house is just south-south-west of here.
I am Heshra. I gut and sell Okeemu's catch here. I run my family. I watch the prices. A buyer does not bargain with me twice.
Okeemu is usually just east of here. Okeemu is too soft to ask what a catch is worth, so I do the selling.
Go south, past the house. It is a fair way. The cooking fire is there.
It is you, my friend. I practised with my stick today. Nobody laughed.
Oh. Hello. I am helping with the nets, so I cannot talk for long.
I do not know you. What do you want?
The boat is just there, north-north-east of here. You can see it.
I am Pip. Okeemu and Heshra are my parents. I help them with the nets. I am going to be a guard. I practise with this stick.
I watch the guards. Raxa-Tum, the guard at the north landing, is usually just north-east of here. Raxa-Tum is the best guard.
Go north a short way. Black Rose Jail is there.
You again, my friend. Good. The path is quiet, so stay a while.
Keep your hand clear of your weapon. Then say what you want.
The dock is just east-south-east of here. You will see a rowing boat just south-east.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the old rising against the Empire. I guard a path. I do not tell tales.
They call me Holds-Fast. I was the last one standing in a brawl on the docks. The name stayed. I guard the south path. I would rather be feared than liked.
Ten-Coins guards between the south docks and the market. He is usually just north-north-east of here. He will hang one day.
The cooking fire? It is just east of here, in plain sight. Walk straight towards it.
At last I know your name. Stand easy. I do not say that to many.
I do not know you. State your name and your business. Spell the name if it is unusual.
This is Black Rose. The dock is just south-east of here.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Black Rose and Lilmoth. I know Lilmoth. It is a midden.
I am Mireel. I came to Black Rose from Lilmoth and stayed. The guard took me because I can read. I keep the duty rolls for the south docks.
Holds-Fast is usually just south-south-east of here, on this same path. He is a brute, but a useful one.
Black Rose Jail? Walk north a short way, and it is there. I give this way free.
Ah, there you are. Stand with me a while. Today I will name you no price.
Keep your purse close, stranger. Then we will get on well.
You want something from me? Most things here have a price. Mine is always fair.
This is Black Rose. The house is just north-east of here. The market's cooking fire is just east of here.
Ask Xuth-Ma about the Rose and its families. He gives that away for nothing. I give nothing away.
I am Ten-Coins. The name is the price of looking away. Everyone knows it at the docks. I call it a fee, and I call it a fair one.
Okaw-Sei is a guard like me, on the dock walk below the market. You will usually find him just east-south-east of here.
The cooking fire is just south-south-west of here, in plain sight. Walk straight to it.
The dock is quiet. You may stand with me, if you wish.
This dock is watched. Say who you are and why you are here.
I stand on the east dock of Black Rose. There is a house just north-west of me, and a boat just south-east. I keep watch between them.
Ask Watches-The-Road about the town's old war with the Empire. A deserter taught me the sword, not the town's history.
I am Corvane, guard of the east dock and of the big ship moored past it. I took my name from a deserter who taught me the sword. We came to Black Rose together. I stayed after he left.
Pitch-Pot seals the boats at this dock. He works harder than anyone on the docks. You will usually find him just east-south-east of me.
The jail? Walk north-west a short way, and Black Rose Jail is there. Mind my pot as you go!
I smell of pitch, I know, but I am glad to see you! Come close.
Mind your feet. The pitch is hot. You will smell me before you see me.
Stand back from the pot or you will be burned. What do you want?
I seal hulls here, so I can tell you about boats. The big ship is just east-south-east of here. A boat lies just south-east.
Ask Sakeeth about the old talk that Black Rose had fallen! I know tar, leaks and rot. She knows the rest.
They call me Pitch-Pot. I got the name as a hatchling, when I fell into the pot. I have smelled of tar ever since.
Corvane is the guard on the east dock. He is a good sort. He is usually just west-north-west of here.
The cooking fire? Go south, a short way. It is there.
The next mat can wait. Sit by me a while.
Mind the reed. I am counting mats.
I live in the house by the road, just north of here.
Ask Counts-The-Tolls about the crossing and its owings. I pay mine in mats. It is the ledger I mind, not the work.

Never-Sold has put money aside to buy a woman out of her Owing on the estate north of Blackrose. She is looking for someone to lend a hand. I know what an Owing weighs. Look for Never-Sold in the Chainbreakers' house, in the north district.
I am Pays-In-Reeds. I weave mats and baskets from marsh reed. I make one mat a day, and that pays my owing. I am working toward my last mat.
Skink is the child who plays by the jail's standing stone. You will find that child just west-north-west of here. That child should be in a home, not out by a jail.
Black Rose Jail? It is a short way north-west of here. Go that way and you will reach it.
My hands will keep working, but I am glad of the company. Sit a while.
Yes? Mind the net, please. I am in the middle of a knot.
This is Black Rose, the market dock. The cooking fire is just west-south-west of here. A boat lies just south-south-west.
Ask Raxa-Tum about Lilmoth. I was born here and have never left, so I can tell you nothing of it.
I am Lux Ha. I mend the nets that come off the market boats. There is always more to mend. I was born in Black Rose and have never left it.
You will usually find Nuxi-Ra, the street vendor at the market, just north of here.
Walk south-west a short way, until the longboat is on your left. Then go along the boards, just west. The cooking fire is there.
Few people come out this far. You are always welcome, my friend. Sit by the water.
Yes? Say what you want.
You are on my dock. Speak, then.
The dock is just south-east of here. My house is just north.
Ask Keeps-The-Stone about the fox-folk. It is not mine to tell. I live at the edge for the quiet.
There is smoke from the stone house just west of my dock. People are shut inside it, and Third-Born Tsaxi keeps the door.
I am Ree-Shaal. I fish from this dock and live in the house behind it.
I moved out to the edge to be away from the town. I like the quiet. Visitors spoil it.
Sleeps-Standing, the guard at the far east dock, is usually just south-east of here. Go and talk to him.
The cooking fire? Climb west a short way, until the longboat is on your left. Then go along the boards just west. The cooking fire is there.
Hnn. Come, stand with me. Nothing is happening here, and I like it better with you.
Hnn. Yes? Speak. I am listening.
Hm. What is it? Say it plainly.
The dock is just east-south-east of here. The house is just west-south-west. There is not much else to see. I prefer it that way.
Ask Talks-To-Water about Red Bramman. I only stand a post, and I would sooner sleep.
Hnn. Smoke rises from the stone house west-north-west of here. Third-Born Tsaxi stands at its door. People are shut in there.
I am Sleeps-Standing. I guard the dock at the eastern edge of Black Rose, where nothing happens. I have learned to sleep on my feet. I wake quickly when I must.
Ree-Shaal, the fisher at the far east dock? Usually just north-west of here. Ree-Shaal is a sour one. Ree-Shaal complains about me. Hnn.
Follow the boards west a short way, past the longboat. The cooking fire is there.
You are a welcome sight after a day of crates. Sit a moment, if you can.
Yes. What do you want?
The big ship is just west of here. I live in the house just north-east of here, by its berth.
Ask Tzeel-Vaa about those who come to Black Rose and stay. I came on a ship myself. I have not decided yet if I was wise to stay.
I am Ojeel. I unload the big ship whenever it comes in. I live in the house by its berth. I signed on to a crew once and walked off it here.
Tadpole, the child who plays around the big ships, is usually just south of here. That child should be kept off the ships.
The cooking fire? Go along the boards north-west a short way, past the longboat. Then you are at the fire. It is easy.
Did you see the ship? Is it still there? I kept watch while you were gone.
Who are you? Are you here to see the ships? Did you drop a coin? I will look for it if you did.
This is the east docks. The big ship is just west-north-west of here, in plain sight. The dock is just north-west. I know every board of it.
I am Tadpole. I play between the big ships and run errands for the crews. One day I will sail on one. Then you will hear of me. What is your name?
Ojeel? He unloads the big ship. He is usually just north of here. He chases me off the ship every time, so do not say I sent you.
Haven? Walk south-east a short way, until you reach the stone tower. Then walk south-west a short way. Haven is there.
The cooking fire? Walk east a fair way. You will find it there.
The next fish will not be long, so sit by the fire.
Come near the fire and tell me what you need.
The fish is still on the fire. Say what you want.
You are standing in my smoke. Speak, or buy something.
My cooking fire is just west-south-west of here, outside the west gate. The tower is just north of here.
Ask Talks-To-Water about the old bandit king. I know fish and smoke. That tale takes longer than a fish.
For news of the road toward Haven, ask Tzeel-Vaa. He is the only honest guard at the west gate, so he will tell it straight.

I am Ahkeeh. I smoke fish over this fire outside the west gate. I sell it to the guards and to anyone coming in by road. I was born on a boat and came ashore when it sank. I have not been on the water since.
Tzeel-Vaa is a guard at the west gate, and I trust him. You will usually find him just south-east of here.

take: I liked the setup: Never-Sold sends me to the Soulrest docks, I hear Heavy-Rope and Ussa-Rekh, and I have to pick a side. The Owing and buy-out ideas were clear, and it tied back to my earlier choice about Rows-For-Another. I sided with Ussa-Rekh because his argument was that unpaid berths mean no more people get bought out. It felt like a real dilemma, though I only skimmed it. The ending was buggy. My Speechcraft was 15 against a 30 check. Paying the 50 gold got a reply from Heavy-Rope but did nothing visible: no gold change I could see and no journal update. The other Speechcraft 30 option, which looked the same as the first, worked at 15 and Heavy-Rope agreed to work the season. Even so, the objective stayed open and Ussa-Rekh had nothing more to say. I could not tell whether the quest was finished, so I stopped. I would want to know what Ussa-Rekh and Never-Sold make of the result, and whether the held people actually benefit.
answers:
1. I think I'm meant to go back to Never-Sold and report how Soulrest went, since the objective at Soulrest never closed and Ussa-Rekh has nothing left to say. I didn't actually try that, so it's a guess. If the quest is done, the journal should say so, and it didn't.

2. Nominally the Chainbreakers, through Never-Sold. She buys out Owings and takes the work as repayment, and she sent me to Soulrest. In practice, I sided with Ussa-Rekh, so I acted for the broker's idea that a season agreed gets worked. I'm not sure Never-Sold sees it that way, since she warned me last time that the next person held would pay for it.

3. The most confusing moment was the persuasion and payment sequence. My Speechcraft was 15 against a 30 check, yet one of the two "30" options worked at 15. The 50 gold got a reply but showed no visible change and no journal update. I couldn't tell whether I'd paid, whether the check had succeeded, or whether the quest was resolved. After Heavy-Rope agreed, the objective stayed open.

4. I'd tell the writer that the dilemma is good and ties back to Rows-For-Another, but the resolution needs clear feedback. Show the gold leaving, show the skill check result, and update the journal when someone agrees. If two options look identical but behave differently, label the difference. Also close the objective, or point me to who to report to, so I know whether I'm finished. I'd like to hear Ussa-Rekh's and Never-Sold's reactions, and learn whether the held people benefit.
